seo.title: Cars.com: Carson AI search engine and dealer monetization - results-to-listing conversion +30% (2025)
seo.meta_description: Cars.com launched Carson, a natural-language AI search engine: +30% conversion from results to listings, and AI building blocks sold to dealers (89% of revenue).
seo.resume_citable: On November 6, 2025, Cars.com launched Carson, a multilingual natural-language AI search engine that assists about 15% of web and mobile web searches and improves conversion from results pages to vehicle detail pages by nearly 30%; AI serves the monetization of a marketplace where about 89% of the record $182 million Q3 2025 revenue comes from subscribing dealers, to whom Cars.com also sells AI building blocks such as inventory video (twice the lead conversion).

faq.q: What is Carson, Cars.com's AI search engine?
faq.a: Carson is a multilingual AI search engine launched on November 6, 2025 that turns a natural-language query into targeted results, in place of filters. It assists about 15% of web and mobile web searches; its users return twice as often, save three times as many vehicles, and convert nearly 30% better from results pages to vehicle detail pages.

faq.q: How does AI serve Cars.com's monetization?
faq.a: Cars.com is a marketplace whose revenue comes mostly from subscribing dealers ($162 million out of $181.6 million in Q3 2025 revenue, or about 89%). The Carson engine makes the marketplace perform better on the buyer side, and Cars.com packages its AI capabilities into solutions sold to dealers, such as AI-Powered Inventory Video, which shows twice the lead conversion of standard video.

Yes. Carson was launched in November 2025 with a mobile app rollout in pilot in Q4 2025, and Cars.com announced four new AI solutions for dealers on January 29, 2026, which confirms the continuity of the strategy.

pattern: Marketplace AI building blocks monetized on both sides: conversational search on the buyer side for conversion, and generation and AI tools packaged and sold to subscribing dealers.
objectif_business: Turn AI into a monetization lever for an auto marketplace where about 89% of revenue comes from subscribing dealers. Cars.com uses the Carson engine on the buyer side to make its marketplace perform better (more engagement, better conversion from results to vehicle detail pages), which strengthens the value sold to dealers, then packages its AI building blocks into paid solutions offered to those same dealers to generate more leads and profit.
description: Cars.com operates a US auto marketplace whose revenue comes mostly from subscribing dealers ($162 million out of $181.6 million in Q3 2025 revenue, or about 89%). On November 6, 2025, it launched Carson, a multilingual AI search engine that turns a natural-language query (for example a reliable, affordable vehicle for a family of five) into targeted results, in place of filters. More than 70% of visitors start their search with no make or model in mind, which Carson is meant to unlock. On the buyer side, Cars.com quantifies the effect: Carson assists about 15% of web and mobile web searches, its users return twice as often, save three times as many vehicles, and convert nearly 30% better from results pages to vehicle detail pages. CEO Alex Vetter summarized the impact on the Q3 2025 earnings call by pointing to a doubling of visitor engagement. On the monetization side, Cars.com turns these AI capabilities into products sold to its dealers: on January 29, 2026, it announced four solutions including AI-Powered Inventory Video, which generates vehicle-specific video ads and shows twice the lead conversion of standard video. The number of subscribing dealers reached 19,526 in Q3 2025, a three-year high, and dealer revenue returned to growth (up 2% year over year) in the record-revenue quarter.
points_cles: Cars.com launched Carson, a multilingual natural-language AI search engine, on November 6, 2025.
Carson assists about 15% of web and mobile web searches and lifts conversion from results pages to vehicle detail pages by about 30%.
AI serves monetization: about 89% of the record $182 million Q3 2025 revenue comes from subscribing dealers.
The AI building blocks are packaged and sold to dealers (AI-Powered Inventory Video, twice the lead conversion).

resultats.metrique: Share of web and mobile web searches assisted by Carson
Improvement in the conversion rate from search results pages (SRP) to vehicle detail pages (VDP) for Carson users
Vehicles saved by Carson users compared to other shoppers
Return visits to Cars.com by Carson users compared to other shoppers
Record quarterly revenue and dealer revenue growth, Q3 2025
Carson's effect on visitor engagement, cited by the CEO on the Q3 2025 earnings call
Lead conversion of the AI-Powered Inventory Video solution sold to dealers, versus traditional video

niveau_preuve.justification: The monetization figures come from Exhibit 99.1 of the 8-K filed with the SEC for Q3 2025 (record revenue of $182 million, dealer revenue of $162 million, dealer growth of 2%, 19,526 dealers), an uninterpreted primary document. The Carson and dealer-solution metrics come from official brand press releases published on cars.com. Three concordant T1 sources, including a financial filing.

stack_technique.detail: Cars.com's multilingual AI search engine, launched November 6, 2025, which turns natural-language queries (for example a need for a reliable, affordable vehicle for a family) into targeted results, replacing filter-based navigation. Deployed on web and mobile web, with the mobile app rollout in pilot in Q4 2025.
A solution that generates VIN-specific video ads with audience targeting, sold to dealers; presented as driving twice the lead conversion on their site compared to traditional video creation.
Cars Commerce's appraisal and trade-in solution, integrated into the dealer offering; more than one million quarterly appraisals in Q3 2025.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Real time on the buyer side (Carson answers search queries in every session); per campaign on the dealer side (inventory video generation per vehicle); conversion and dealer revenue tracked quarter over quarter.
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: Cars Commerce's product and data teams operate Carson and the AI solutions sold; subscribing dealers activate and run the AI products they buy (inventory video, market expansion).
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: Conversion from results pages to vehicle detail pages, and lead conversion on the dealer side. If the indexed inventory (listings, prices, photos) degrades, the relevance of Carson's answers and therefore conversion drop, and the value sold to dealers falls with it.

etapes.detail: The visitor describes their need in plain language (budget, use, reliability) instead of handling filters; more than 70% arrive with no make or model in mind.

etapes.etape: AI interprets and returns targeted results
etapes.detail: Carson interprets the query and returns a tailored results page, with summaries (award-winning vehicles, made-in-America index), to drive the click toward vehicle detail pages.

etapes.etape: Conversion to the vehicle detail page and the dealer
etapes.detail: The buyer moves from results to the vehicle detail page and then to the dealer; Cars.com measures SRP-to-VDP conversion, saves, and leads.

etapes.etape: Packaging the AI building blocks into sold solutions
etapes.detail: Cars Commerce turns its AI capabilities into paid products (VIN-level inventory video, market-area expansion, reporting) offered to subscribing dealers.
The dealer subscribes and activates the AI solution on their inventory; the revenue flows into dealer revenue, which accounts for about 89% of the group's revenue.

prerequis_data: A rich, clean inventory catalog (listings, prices, photos, features) that can be indexed for natural-language search
A first-party history of search behavior to frame the relevance of results
Reliable measurement of conversion from results pages to product pages and to the lead, before and after
prerequis_orga: A marketplace business model where most revenue comes from subscribing sellers, not from a margin on transactions
A product and data team able to operate a conversational engine in production and to package AI building blocks into commercial offers
A sales force able to sell and operate these AI solutions with sellers
A compliance framework for AI transparency (AI Act) and the GDPR legal basis for personalization
stack_possible: An in-house conversational search engine coupled with an LLM and an inventory index
A per-listing video creative generator for sellers
replication.equipe: AI engineers (conversational engine, inventory index, video generation), a marketplace product team, a data team for conversion measurement, a sales and success team to sell and operate the solutions with sellers, and a GDPR and AI Act compliance function involved on an ongoing basis.

playbook.action: Index the inventory (listings, prices, photos, attributes) to enable reliable, multilingual natural-language search.
playbook.livrable: An inventory index queryable by a conversational assistant.

playbook.action: Deploy a conversational search engine on the buyer side on a high-volume surface, with transparency about its AI nature.
playbook.livrable: Engine in production, results traceable to the source inventory.

playbook.action: Measure conversion from results pages to product pages and to the lead, on the equipped surface against the old path.
playbook.livrable: Before-and-after conversion reading, decision to extend or stop.

playbook.action: Package the AI capabilities into paid solutions for sellers (per-listing video generation, market-area expansion, reporting).
playbook.livrable: A commercial offering of AI building blocks that subscribing sellers can activate.

playbook.action: Track the effect on seller revenue and lead conversion to justify pricing and expand the solutions catalog.
playbook.livrable: Reading of the incremental seller revenue attributable to the AI solutions.

replication.premiere_etape: Connect a conversational search engine to the existing inventory of a single high-volume surface, and measure conversion from results pages to product pages against the old filter-based path, before turning it into a building block sold to sellers.

statut_vivant.note: Carson launched November 6, 2025 with the mobile app rollout in pilot in Q4 2025, already at about 15% of web searches. The AI solutions sold to dealers were announced on January 29, 2026, which confirms the continuity of the deployment and the monetization strategy less than six months before verification.

transposable_ue.note: Cars.com is a purely American auto marketplace, but the setup is transposable to a European auto marketplace (leboncoin, La Centrale, AutoScout24, mobile.de): multilingual conversational search on the buyer side to improve conversion from results pages to vehicle detail pages, and AI building blocks (inventory video generation, market-area expansion) packaged and sold to subscribing dealers. EU constraints: AI Act transparency about the fact that the user is interacting with an AI in the search engine (Carson is already multilingual, which simplifies the adaptation), and a GDPR legal basis for personalization based on search behavior. The data used on the buyer side is mostly inventory content (vehicle listings, prices), not sensitive personal data, which makes the transposition easier.
